messages.text: (The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Hi Winson, I'm Hal, HeliumDeploy's technical specialist.

In your photo the Thor P2 is on its green stand with the big front fan lit up blue, so the miner has power. You've circled the small fan on the end of the power supply, next to where the cable plugs in.

What's going on with that fan?

1. It isn't spinning at all
2. It's loud, rattling or buzzing
3. The power supply feels very hot
4. Something else

If you can, also tell me whether the miner is already hashing (does its screen or web page show a hashrate?) or whether you've only just plugged it in.

If you notice a burning smell, sparks or a hot plug, unplug it straight away and tell me.
the fan not working
Searched the web · Hammer Thor P2 power supply fan not spinning

Thanks, Winson. A power supply fan that isn't spinning isn't always a fault. On many power supplies like this one the fan only switches on once the unit warms up under load, so it can sit still for a while after you plug it in. I can't confirm from the specs that this particular power supply works that way, so let's check it on yours.

Your photo shows the miner's big fan running, so the power supply is giving it power. The question is whether the small fan starts once the miner is working hard.

**Next step:**

1. Make sure the Thor P2 is actually mining: its screen or web page should show a hashrate above zero.
2. Let it run like that for about 20 minutes, with space around the power supply so air can get in and out.
3. Then check the small fan again. Is it spinning now? And does the power supply feel warm, or too hot to keep your hand on?

Please don't open the power supply or poke anything through the grille.

If it gets very hot while the fan is still stopped, or you smell burning, unplug it straight away and tell me.

What do you see after the 20 minutes? If the miner isn't mining yet, tell me what its screen shows and I'll help you get it set up first.

Hi Sarah,

The miner has been running for 15 minutes now, and it is operating normally with a hashrate of 9.2 TH/s.

However, the black power supply box feels warm, but its small cooling fan is still not spinning.

Could you please advise whether this is normal or if there might be an issue with the fan?

Thank you.
Handed to the team · No product facts on whether the Thor P2 PSU fan is thermostatic or should always

I'm not able to confirm whether the fan on this power supply should be spinning at this load, so I've sent it to JD, our hardware lead (by the way, I'm Hal, the technical specialist, not Sarah). Someone will pick up your ticket and get back to you by email, usually within one business day. You don't need to stay in the chat.

The good news is that 9.2 TH/s is a healthy hashrate for the Thor P2. A power supply that is warm but not hot is not a reason to stop.

Until you hear back:

1. You can keep mining.
2. Keep space around the power supply so air can flow, and don't cover it.
3. Every so often, touch it to check. If it becomes too hot to keep your hand on, or you smell burning, unplug it straight away.

For a quicker answer, you can also ask in our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and mention @nullhashrate (that's JD). He and the community are very active there.

Regarding the power cable, the original cable supplied has a 3-pin US plug. I requested a Malaysian plug, which should be a Type G (UK-style 3-pin plug), but the cable I received has a different plug. i get in the box is type C - EUROPEAN 2-OIN PLUG

I've passed the wrong plug on order Shop···· to Sarah in support, and she'll answer your plug message here. You asked for a Malaysian Type G plug but got a European 2-pin cable.

Your earlier question about the power supply fan is with JD, our hardware lead. Someone will get back to you on that by email, and your Thor P2 is fine to keep mining at 9.2 TH/s in the meantime. If the power supply gets too hot to touch or you smell burning, unplug it straight away.
is that normal can support ?

Hi Winson, I'm Hal, HeliumDeploy's technical specialist.

There are two separate things here, so here's an answer on each.

**1. The power supply fan not spinning**
I can't confirm yet whether that's normal for this power supply, so JD, our hardware lead, has your question. Your Thor P2 at 9.2 TH/s is healthy, and a power supply that's warm but not hot is fine to keep running. Keep space around it, and unplug it straight away if it gets too hot to touch or smells of burning.

For a quicker answer, you can ask in our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and mention @nullhashrate (that's JD).

**2. The European 2-pin cable**
Please don't push the 2-pin plug into a Malaysian socket by force or with a loose travel adapter. A miner draws power all day, and a poor connection can heat up. The safe options are:

1. A Malaysian power cord with a Type G plug that fits the socket on your power supply. Electronics shops sell these locally.
2. A good-quality, fused Type G adapter that grips the plug firmly. Check now and then that it isn't getting warm.

Sarah already has the wrong plug on your order, and she asked you for a photo of the cable, showing both the plug and the end that goes into the power supply. If you send that here, I can also tell you which type of cord to buy locally.
yes, pls tell me which type G plug i should buy. and what power V

I can't tell yet exactly which cord fits, because it depends on two things printed on or built into your power supply. Here is how to check both.

**1. Voltage**
Malaysia's mains power is 240 V. Look at the label on the black power supply for the line marked **"Input"**. If it says something like **100-240V ~ 50/60Hz**, it works fine on Malaysian power and you don't need a converter, only the right cord. If the input range on the label doesn't include 240 V, don't plug it in, and tell me.

**2. The socket on the power supply** (where the cord plugs in)
Check what shape it is:
1. **3 holes in a flat-topped shape** (like a PC or monitor): buy a Type G cord with a **C13** end. This is the common "computer power cord".
2. **3 round holes like a cloverleaf** ("Mickey Mouse"): buy a Type G cord with a **C5** end.
3. **2 holes in a figure-8 shape**: buy a Type G cord with a **C7** end.

When you buy the cord:
- Choose one with a **SIRIM** mark (Malaysia's safety approval), a proper Type G 3-pin plug with a built-in fuse.
- The cord's current rating (in amps) should be at least the input current printed on your power supply's label.

The easiest way is to send me a clear photo of the power supply's label and of the socket where the cord goes in. I'll read them and tell you exactly which cord to buy.
SRY, i wan to double comfimed, THOR P2, in malaysia i need use TYPE G PLUG CORRECT ?

Yes, that's correct. In Malaysia the wall sockets take a **Type G** plug, the 3-pin UK-style one with three rectangular pins. The plug depends on the country's sockets, not on the miner, so for the Thor P2 in Malaysia you need a cord with a Type G plug.

Before you buy, check two things:
1. **The other end of the cord** has to match the socket on your power supply (C13, C5 or C7, as in my last message).
2. **The label on the power supply** should show an input range that includes 240 V, for example "100-240V".

If you send me a photo of the power supply's label and its socket, I'll tell you exactly which cord to buy.
so the plug u gave me now, is tyPE C - european 2-pin can use also ? what is the different. will it damage the device ?

Good question. The difference is the shape of the plug, not the electricity.

**What's the difference**
- **Type C (European)** has 2 round pins and no earth pin.
- **Type G (Malaysia/UK)** has 3 rectangular pins: live, neutral and earth, with a fuse inside the plug.
- Europe uses 230 V and Malaysia uses 240 V, which is almost the same. The plug shape doesn't change the voltage. The voltage comes from your wall socket.

**Will it damage the Thor P2?**
Not on its own, as long as the power supply label shows an input range that includes 240 V (for example "100-240V"). If it doesn't, don't plug it in, and tell me.

**Can you use the 2-pin cord?**
It won't fit a Malaysian socket on its own, so you'd need an adapter. The risks come from the connection, not from the miner:
1. A cheap or loose adapter can heat up, because the miner draws power 24 hours a day.
2. The 2-pin cord has no earth connection.

So:
- **For now:** it's OK to use it with a good-quality, fused Type G adapter that grips the pins firmly. Touch the adapter now and then. If it feels warm or hot, unplug it.
- **For the long term:** a proper SIRIM-approved Type G cord is the safer choice.

Please don't push the 2-pin plug straight into a Malaysian socket or wedge something in the earth hole.

The wrong cord in your box is with Sarah on the order side, so she'll come back to you about that.
i saw the plug u gave me is 2.5A 250V. SO i just need to buy malaysia type G SAME power right

Yes, almost. 2.5A 250V is the rating printed on the cord that came in the box. Here's what to match when you buy the Malaysian one:

1. **Plug:** Type G (Malaysian 3-pin), SIRIM-approved.
2. **Rating:** **at least 2.5A, 250V.** A higher rating is fine, for example a cord rated 5A or 10A with a 3A or 5A fuse in the plug. Lower than 2.5A is not.
3. **The other end:** the same shape as the end of the cord you have now, the end that goes into the power supply. Easiest is to take your current cord to the shop and show them.
   - 2 holes, figure-8 shape = **C7**
   - 3 holes, cloverleaf = **C5**
   - 3 holes, flat-topped = **C13**

With that, the Thor P2 gets exactly the same power as before. Only the plug shape changes.
ok. 5A also can be support

Yes, a 5A cord is fine. The amp rating is the most the cord can carry safely. Your Thor P2 only draws the power it needs, so a cord rated higher than 2.5A won't push more power into it and won't damage anything. It just has more safety margin.

What matters:
1. **Type G plug**, SIRIM-approved
2. **2.5A or higher** (5A is good), **250V**
3. **The same end** as your current cord, the end that goes into the power supply

If the fuse in the plug is 3A or 5A, that's also fine.
ok. but now i using my type c u gave me is fine also right. because is same 2.5A 250V

Yes. The cord itself is fine. Its 2.5A 250V rating is enough for the Thor P2, and the power is the same.

The only thing to watch is how it goes into your Malaysian wall socket:

1. **Good:** through a proper Type G adapter (ideally fused) that holds the 2-pin plug firmly with no wobble.
2. **Not OK:** pushed straight into the socket, forced, or with something wedged in the earth hole.

While you use it this way, touch the adapter now and then. If it feels warm or hot, or the plug is loose, unplug it and switch to a Malaysian Type G cord.
OK. can i use the orginal plug UK ?

Thanks for the photo, Winson. One correction first: the cord labelled "Original" has a **US plug (Type B)**, not a UK one. It has two flat pins and one round earth pin. A UK/Malaysian Type G plug has three rectangular pins. The European 2-pin cord is the one lying on the table behind it.

The photo also answers the cord question: the end that goes into your power supply is a **figure-8 (C7)** connector, with 2 holes and no earth. So:

1. **Either cord works the same way.** The US plug's round earth pin isn't connected to anything at the power supply end, so the US cord is no safer than the European one.
2. **Neither fits a Malaysian socket directly.** Each needs a good, firmly fitting Type G adapter, as we discussed. Please don't force either one into the wall.
3. **What to buy for the long term:** a **"Type G to C7 (figure-8)" power cord**, SIRIM-approved, rated **2.5A or higher, 250V**. It's a very common cord in Malaysian electronics shops (the same one used for many TVs and laptop chargers). Show the shop this photo of the figure-8 end.
okay. maybe i can use to plug convert with use the US plug type. maybe the small cooling fan will working ?

Yes, you can use the US cord with a good Type G adapter that grips it firmly. It's just as safe as the European cord, no better and no worse.

But changing the cord **won't make the small fan start**. Both cords carry the same 240 V from your wall socket to the same figure-8 input, and the power supply sees no difference. Whether that fan spins is decided inside the power supply, so the cord doesn't affect it.

The fan question is still with JD, our hardware lead, and he'll get back to you by email. Your Thor P2 is fine to keep running at 9.2 TH/s in the meantime. If the power supply ever gets too hot to keep your hand on, or you smell burning, unplug it straight away.
ok. i will use type c 1st from the box. because is same 2.5A 250V

Sounds good. Using the Type C cord from the box is fine. Just remember:

1. Plug it in through a good Type G adapter that grips it firmly.
2. Every so often, touch the adapter. If it feels warm or loose, unplug it.

Later on, a Type G to C7 (figure-8) cord, 2.5A or higher, will let you go without the adapter.

Your fan question is still with JD, and he'll reply to you by email.
OK NOTED. I MUST BUY TYPE G TO C7, this is suitable for THOR P2

Yes, a **Type G to C7 (figure-8)** cord is the right one for your Thor P2's power supply in Malaysia. When you buy it, check that:

1. It's **SIRIM-approved**.
2. It's rated **2.5A or higher, 250V** (5A is fine).
3. The figure-8 end fits your power supply the same way your current cord does.

You don't have to buy it. The Type C cord from the box with a good adapter works fine for now. The Type G cord just lets you plug straight into the wall without the adapter.

The wrong cord in your box is still with Sarah on the order side.

If the video is too large to send here, the photo of the label and your answer about the heat are enough to start with.

Searched the web · Hammer Thor P2 BM1373 default frequency core voltage

I couldn't find Hammer's published factory values for the Thor P2's frequency and voltage, so I can't tell you for sure whether 720 MHz and 226 are the factory numbers. I won't guess.

What I can tell you is that your miner is behaving normally. The Thor P2 
uses two BM1373 chips and pushes approximately 10 TH/s
, and your 9.2 TH/s is right in that range.

Two questions so I know where those numbers came from:

1. **Did you change them, or were they already set** when you first opened the settings page?
2. **What chip temperature** does the screen or web page show?

If you haven't changed anything, it's best to leave them as they are. Settings the stock firmware set itself are normal use. Raising the frequency or voltage above that is overclocking, which you do at your own risk. It can push the temperature up, and any damage it causes may not be covered by the warranty.

For an exact answer on the Thor P2's factory values, JD can confirm on the Discord: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf (mention @nullhashrate). Your video and the power supply label photo are still welcome here whenever they're ready.

Reading the label now. I'll quickly check whether this model's fan is temperature-controlled.
Searched the web · GM-H250S12 power supply fan

Thanks, Winson, the label is clear. Here's what it says:

- **Model:** GM-H250S12, a 12 V switching power supply made by Shenzhen Qilink Tech.
- **Input:** 176-264V AC (47-63Hz) gives the full **12V 25A** output. 100-176V AC gives 12V 20.8A.
- **Fan:** the label lists a "20CFM Fan".

What this means for you:

1. **Voltage is fine.** Malaysia's 240 V is inside the 176-264 V range, so the power supply runs at its full rating on your mains.
2. **It has plenty of headroom.** 12 V × 25 A is about 300 W, while the Thor P2 uses approximately 166W at the wall. So the power supply is running at only about half its cap····, which is probably why it feels just warm.
3. **About the fan:** the label confirms there is a fan, but it doesn't say whether it only switches on when the power supply gets hot. I couldn't find this model's fan behaviour published anywhere either. I'll add your photo and the model name to the question JD already has, so he can confirm whether a still fan is normal for this model.

At half load and only warm, it's fine to keep mining. The short video of the still fan is still useful whenever you can send it. As before, if the power supply gets too hot to keep your hand on, or you smell burning, unplug it.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)
Handed to the team · Customer is on 240V Malaysia mains. Miner screen after 1h30m: 9.33 TH/s, Vin 11.

I've opened your screen photo. Your Thor P2 looks very healthy after 1 hour 30 minutes:

- **Hashrate:** 9.33 TH/s, right where it should be.
- **Power:** Vin 11.9V is a steady 12 V from the power supply, and the board is drawing 134.2W. The power supply is rated around 300 W, so it has lots of spare cap····.
- **Temperatures:** chip 44.8°C and the voltage regulator (TPS) 64.8°C. Both are comfortable.
- **Miner fan:** 2075 rpm at 100%, so it's cooling properly.
- **Vo 2.25V:** this is the "226" you saw in the settings. The screen shows the actual voltage it's running at, and it matches.

So the power supply is delivering clean, stable power even with its small fan still. I've added your power supply model (GM-H250S12) and these readings to the question JD has. Someone will pick up your ticket and get back to you by email to confirm whether a still fan is normal for this model.

You can keep mining as it is. If you still make the short video of the power supply fan, send it here and I'll pass it on too.

Yes, please send the video here in the chat. 10 to 20 seconds showing the still fan is enough. If it won't upload because it's too large, a shorter clip works too.

While you're there, quickly touch the power supply. After more than an hour, does it still feel just warm, or is it getting hot?

Your readings so far look healthy, so you can keep solo mining in the meantime. If it ever gets too hot to keep your hand on, or you smell burning, unplug it.

Thanks for posting the video in the Discord, JD can see it there.

"Warm hot" could mean a few things, so let's do one quick check: **put your palm flat on the top of the power supply and hold it there for 5 seconds.**

1. **You can hold it for 5 seconds easily:** that's normal for a power supply under load. Keep mining.
2. **You have to pull your hand away before 5 seconds:** unplug the power supply from the wall now and let it cool. Then tell me, and I'll update JD that it's running too hot with the fan still.

Whichever it is, it helps to keep the power supply on a hard surface with space around it, not under or behind the miner and not covered.
